items.title: Hunting Vulnerabilities in PHP with LLMs
items.summary: Talk given at the IPC Munich September 2027Hackers are already using Large Language Models to map your attack surface, it’s time you used them to defend it.While we’ve spent years trying to write the perfect regex or rule-set to catch bugs, LLMs have unlocked a terrifyingly effective ability to understand the intent and context of our Symfony and PHP code.This session dives into the practical reality of using AI as an autonomous security researcher to uncover deep-seated vulnerabilities in Symfony applications that traditional tools simply cannot see.We will explore how to architect a high-speed security pipeline that feeds your codebase to an LLM to detect broken access control, complex injection paths, and logic flaws in real-time.You’ll walk away with a battle-tested strategy to weaponize AI against your own technical debt, turning the most unpredictable technology of our time into your most meticulous security auditor.

items.title: Let the Agent Drive: QA on Android with Trailblaze and the Android CLI
items.summary: Validating a Jira ticket on a real Android device takes thirty minutes on a good day but can be days of hands-on testing when every edge case matters. What if the agent could do it for you?In this session, we'll explore two brand-new tools that make agent-driven Android QA real today: Trailblaze, Block's open-source AI automation framework, and Google's Android CLI v1.0, stable since I/O 2026. We'll see how to chain them with any LLM agent to read a Jira ticket and drive a real device end-to-end like handling Chrome Custom Tabs, app permissions or icon-only buttons along the way.Can it cover everything? Can it really retire manual QA? Let's plug in a Pixel and see how far we get 🤖
